question: Our tree on their bench shape: what does OUR fixed32 stock engine do under sglang's own bench_serving at ISL/OSL 1024/1024?

engine.checkpoint: /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 (conservative arm, bf16 KV, NVFP4 body, BF16 lm_head)
engine.cmdline_parity: byte-identical to the reference arm's PID-1 argv EXCEPT the trailing --middleware flag (dropped, see compromises)
engine.env_parity: 548-var container env diffed against the reference arm: every decode-path variable identical (FIXED32 mode/mask/active/physical, TAIL_MODE, DRAFT_SOURCE, GDN geom, MANDATORY_WEIGHT_BYTES 27977022848, WEIGHT_FLOOR_MS 102.479937172, DRAFT_VOCAB K/ROOT, MAX_NUM_SEQS, ATTENTION_BACKEND, CUDAGRAPH_MODE, ENABLE_APC, timers). Deltas are run-dir paths, container hostname, harness-only campaign/proxy vars, and the middleware flag.

client.note: identical dataset/shape to the pass-11 sglang calibration; ignore_eos on (bench default) so every request emits exactly 1024 tokens

bs8_partial.status: PARTIAL — client stopped at ~5 min to protect the step-2 GPU budget; 4 of 16 requests had completed
bs8_partial.structural_caveat: our stock arm's admission width is max_num_seqs=1, so an 8-way OFFERED load is SERIALIZED (metrics showed running=1 / waiting=7, zero preemptions). This measures queueing, NOT 8-way batch amortization, and is therefore NOT comparable to sglang's 147.78 bs=8 aggregate.

their_reference_pass11.note: sglang container + RadixArk as-shipped + EAGLE 3/1/4, greedy (bench default temperature 0.0)

verdict.reading: On THEIR workload our tree LOSES by ~26%. The mechanism is acceptance, not step cost: our accept/event falls from 4.526 (real SWE agent traffic, 35k contexts) to 2.358 on 1024-token random-token prompts, while our step wall stays ~172 ms. Their EAGLE chain barely notices the workload change (accept 2.90 on the same shape). The tree's 1.9x acceptance premium is a property of PREDICTABLE agentic code traffic; on unpredictable random-token traffic the premium evaporates and the tree's fixed 31-draft verify cost is dead weight.
verdict.triangle: leg1 = their chain / their shape 26.1 · leg2 = our tree / our shape 25.3 · leg3 = our tree / their shape 19.3 · (step 2 = their chain / our shape)

compromises: MIDDLEWARE DROPPED: the stock arm serves with --middleware lumo_flywheel_serving.inference_proxy.Fixed32EngineIngressMiddleware, an ASGI guard that authenticates a per-task HMAC header only the SWE harness mints. bench_serving cannot mint it, so leg 3 ran a one-line-patched COPY of the launcher (scripts/fr14_leg3_launch_nomiddleware.sh) with FR13_FIXED32_MIDDLEWARE_FLAGS="". Nothing else changed; the middleware is an audit guard on ingress, not a decode-path component.

SAMPLING: bench_serving defaults to temperature 0.0. Our fixed32 committer HARD-REFUSES greedy ('FR13 fixed32 requires sampled temp>0, no draft_probs, and max_spec_len=31' — engine died on the first request, twice, logged in ablation_a_leg3_temp0_refusal.txt). Leg 3 therefore ran at OUR deployment sampling profile (temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20), which is also what the 25.3 stock number was measured at. Their pass-11 26.1 was greedy. This is an unavoidable asymmetry: the two stacks cannot be run at the same temperature.

SEQUENCE FILE HEAD-PINNED: a concurrent agent is live-editing scripts/ on this branch (a floor re-derivation that moves FR13_MANDATORY_WEIGHT_BYTES 27977022848 -> 25210209416). Leg 3 sources a HEAD (61e6b98a1) copy of scripts/fr13_fixed32_floor_timers_seq.sh so it reproduces the committed b1-stock arm exactly. src/ was verified unmodified, so the engine's runtime code is HEAD-clean.
BS=8 PARTIAL: see bs8_partial.status. 16 prompts (not 32) were offered to halve the serialized cost, and the client was stopped early.

NO SWE RUNNER: leg 3 is engine-only (no harness, no proxy, no agent). The fixed32 ready-ack / work-census / boundary-flush handshakes the harness normally performs did not run, so the fr13_decode_step_wall_* and fr13_decode_forward_gpu_* counters stayed at 0 (they publish only through the explicit flush transaction). The vLLM-native spec_decode and request_decode counters used above are unaffected.
